name: rokokol-skills
description: Agent skills for writing, checking and shipping software, each in its own repository

plugins.name: 3x-ui-admin
plugins.description: Administer a 3x-ui panel over its HTTP API — inbounds, clients, hosts, master and node links, routing, Xray and panel settings, and subscriptions

plugins.name: ai-commit-trailers
plugins.description: Which AI-disclosure trailer a commit carries — Generated-by, Assisted-by (mostly or partly), or none — and why never Co-authored-by or Signed-off-by for an agent

plugins.name: bash-best-practices
plugins.description: A standard for sh and bash utilities: one script shape, help as the single source of truth, portability to the bash 3.2 macOS ships, and a checker that holds the help to the code

plugins.name: ci
plugins.description: CI that stays green for the right reasons: GitHub Actions conventions, pinned toolchains instead of registry lookups, and weekly cascades that land dependency bumps only on green

plugins.name: close-session
plugins.description: Close a working session: save what it taught where the next session will read it, retire what went stale, and leave nothing hanging

plugins.name: code-comments
plugins.description: What a comment in code says and what it must not: the reader it is written for, the register, the moment it must not be anchored to, and a checker that reads comments out of the syntax tree

plugins.name: companion
plugins.description: A template for an assistant persona and the two dossiers behind it, kept out of the always-loaded instructions and rewritten for whoever adopts it

plugins.name: contributing
plugins.description: Everything published under your GitHub identity, and the homework before it: pushes, issues, pull requests, reviews and comments, each shown and approved one at a time

plugins.name: create-readme
plugins.description: The house rules for a README: structure and tone, one paragraph per line with no hard wrapping, no trailing full stop, and no section that has its own file

plugins.name: huix-standard
plugins.description: Making Nix-flake-first Linux repositories installable on any distribution without Nix: a canonical install.sh, uninstall by manifest, and a dependency preflight that never installs

plugins.name: maintainer-docs
plugins.description: Repository-wide maintainer rationale in WORKAROUNDS.md, DEVIATIONS.md and PITFALLS.md: which file owns a non-obvious fact, and when the explanation belongs beside the code instead

plugins.name: nix-best-practices
plugins.description: A standard for Nix: the scope a with opens, the shape of a module header, what a derivation's meta has to say and what a flake.lock must not hold — everything nixfmt, statix and deadnix cannot see — plus a checker that holds a tree to it

plugins.name: obsidian-cli
plugins.description: Drive a running Obsidian vault from the terminal through the official Obsidian CLI — read and write notes, find one by name, alias, tag or property, and query the link graph

plugins.name: papers
plugins.description: Find, read and compare scientific papers without spending the conversation's context on them: a shortlist for a topic, a bounded digest of one paper, and a comparison of several

plugins.name: skill-authoring
plugins.description: The house rules for text an agent loads whole into a conversation, and check-skill.sh, the gate that proves a skill loadable, its references reachable and its links resolvable

plugins.name: super-productivity
plugins.description: Manage Super Productivity tasks through its Local REST API — list, create, edit, schedule, complete and delete them, run the timer, and report tracked time

plugins.name: tests
plugins.description: Tests that mean something when they are green: a verdict no pipe can swallow, logs read even at exit 0, and every check watched failing before it is trusted

plugins.name: versioning
plugins.description: What a repository says about itself over time: whether it has a version at all, where that version lives, what its changelog looks like, and the ritual that cuts a release
